gen-comfortaa-gf-pontano-sans: Round, friendly letters drawn like glowing neon tubing. Pontano Sans follows with open c terminals and a contemporary sans feel, leaving Comfortaa to supply all the stretched, tube-like drama.
gen-comfortaa-gf-quattrocento-sans: Comfortaa draws every stroke like bent neon tubing. Quattrocento Sans carries the paragraphs in clean modern sans-serif, its gaps keeping c from turning into o, so reading should feel smooth and unhurried.
gen-comfortaa-gf-sarala: A ring-like, wide-open c leads the way. Sarala has a neon-glass thickness and distinct gaps, so extended reading should feel approachable and easy going beneath the stretched-out Comfortaa heading.
gen-comfortaa-gf-stick: Neon-tube roundness, loosely spaced. Stick, a modern sans-serif, keeps constant-weight, tubelike lines with exits wide enough to pass light, so longer text should read steadily and clearly beside Comfortaa.
gen-comfortaa-gf-zen-kaku-gothic-antique: Soft, stretched, and glowing like neon. Zen Kaku Gothic Antique, a modern sans-serif, matches its t crossbar to the stem and curves smoothly, giving Comfortaa a tidy partner on the page.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-taviraj: Blunt, bold, cut from one gauge of tubing. Aaargh is best at stamping out stems and curves in a single gauge, while Taviraj the serif is best at medium-contrast strokes with gentle gaps.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-uchen: Strong, round, and never swelling. Aaargh keeps round bowls with uniform walls and Uchen adds understated stroke contrast, so the headline stays blunt while the text turns dignified and refined.
gen-dafont-aaargh-ibm-plex-serif: IBM Plex Serif arrives with slimmer horizontals and an unclenched c. Under the constant-stroke Aaargh heading, paragraphs in this serif should read steadily and with a quiet, authoritative tone.
gen-dafont-arkhip-gf-cutive: Refined, with letters floating well apart. Arkhip is best at modern, single-thickness strokes and an open c, while Cutive the serif is best at wide-tracked literary running text.
